τῆς συγκρίσεως τῆς πρὸς τὸ ὑπερέχον. 2 Kor 3,11 Ἔδειξεν ὅτι δεῖ παύσασθαι καὶ
ἀργῆσαι τὸν νόμον, ἀντεισαχθεῖσαν δὲ τοῦ πνεύματος τὴν χάριν διαμεῖναι. 2 Kor
3,12–14 Ἔχοντες οὖν τοιαύτην ἐλπίδα. ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς·
ἐδήλωσε δὲ ὅτι μένει ἡ χάρις καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τὰς προσθήκας λαμβάνουσα
πρὸς τὸ μὴ δύνασθαι ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ καταργουμένου·
ὡς γὰρ οὐκ 286 ἠδύνατο τῇ δόξῃ ... προσέχειν, οὕτως οὐκ ἐδύναντο οὐδὲ τῷ τέλει
τοῦ νόμου, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὅτι παυθήσεται ὁ νόμος. αὐτίκα φησίν· ἄχρι σήμερον ἔχουσι
κάλυμμα. τὸ τέλος τοῦ νόμου, ὅταν ἀρθῇ τὸ κάλυμμα καὶ θεάσωνται τὴν δόξαν τοῦ
πνεύματος, ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται, τοῦτ' ἔστι διὰ τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν πίστεως. 285,ξολ2
Ποίαν ἐλπίδα; ὅτι οὐ καταργεῖται ἡ τοῦ πνεύματος χάρις ὥσπερ ὁ νόμος, ἀλλὰ μένει
καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν. Ἡμεῖς διὰ τὴν μακαρίαν ἐλπίδα τοῦ παραμένειν τοῦ
πνεύματος τὴν χάριν μετὰ παρρησίας διδάσκομεν, καὶ οὐ μιμούμεθα τὰ Μωϋσέως
ἐπιτάγματα, ὃς διὰ 286,ξολ2 τοῦ ἐπὶ πρόσωπον καλύμματος ἐσήμανεν ὅτι οὐ
δύνανται ἀτενίσαι καὶ συνιδεῖν Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι τέλος λήψεται καὶ ἀργήσει ὁ νόμος.
Μένει τὸ κάλυμμα μηδὲ ὄψιν δεικνύον ὅτι Χριστοῦ ἐλθόντος καταργεῖται ὁ νόμος. 2
Kor 3,15–16 Ὥσπερ Μωϋσῆς λαλῶν μὲν Ἰουδαίοις εἶχε τὸ κάλυμμα, ὑποστρέφων δὲ
πρὸς κύριον περιαιρεῖται αὐτό, καὶ νῦν Ἰουδαῖοι μετὰ τὸ ἀναγνῶναι τὸν νόμον καὶ
ἀποδοῦναι τὴν βίβλον ἀποφέρουσιν τὸ κάλυμμα ὡς ὑποστρέψαντος Μωϋσέως πρὸς
κύριον. ἐὰν οὖν ἀποστὰς ἔλθῃς πρὸς τὸ πνεῦμα, περιαιρεῖταί σου τὸ κάλυμμα ὥσπερ
καὶ Μωϋσέως ὑποστρέφοντος πρὸς κύριον. 2 Kor 3,17 Ὁ καταξιωθεὶς πνεύματος
κυρίου οὗτος ἠλευθηρώθη τῆς κατακρίσεως τοῦ νόμου· διὰ γὰρ τοῦ πνεύματος
ἐνεργεῖται τὰ χαρίσματα. καὶ ἡ δωρεὰ πρὸς τοὺς ἀξίους. 2 Kor 3,18 Ἡμεῖς, φησίν, οἱ
ἀπόστολοι ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ ὁρώμεθα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· εἰπὼν δὲ ἡμεῖς
πάντες δείκνυσι κοινὴν τοῦ πνεύματος τὴν εὐεργεσίαν. καὶ Μωϋσέως μὲν ἡ δόξα
ἀπρόσιτος ἦν Ἰσραηλίταις, ἡμῶν δὲ ἡ δόξα τοῦ θεοῦ εὐπρόσιτός ἐστιν· στηρίσαντες
γὰρ ἑαυτοὺς τῇ πίστει καὶ καθάραντες κατοπτριζόμεθα τὴν δόξαν τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦτ'
ἔστι καὶ ὁρῶμεν καὶ ἀπομασσόμεθα ὡς ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ ταῖς ψυχαῖς τὴν εἰκόνα τῆς δόξης
τοῦ πνεύματος. ἀπὸ νομικῆς ἐπιστήμης εἰς πνευματικὴν χάριν μεταμορφούμεθα. ἢ
οὕτως νοητέον· ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς ἐνεργουμένης ἐν ἡμῖν ἐρχόμεθα
287,ξολ2 δηλονότι εἰς δόξαν τῆς υἱοθεσίας. τὸ δὲ καθάπερ δηλοῖ ἅτε δὴ ἀπὸ κυρίου
πνεύματος. ἐπιτηρητέον δὲ ὅτι κύριον τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον εἶπεν, οὐχὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ
θεοῦ. καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ μέν τις ὁρᾷ τὸ ἔσοπτρον ἐκεῖνο, ὁ δὲ δέχεται τοῦ ὁρῶντος τὸ
ἴνδαλμα, οὕτω καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ πνεύματος· οἱ γὰρ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ Χριστοῦ
κατοπτριζόμενοι αὐτοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης ὁμοιότητά τινα ἀποφέροντες εἰς δόξαν, τοῦτ'
ἔστιν ἐπισπῶνται καὶ λαμβάνουσι δόξαν τῆς πνευματικῆς εἰκόνος. 286.30
Μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ νομικῆς ἐπιστήμης εἰς πνευματικὴν χάριν, καὶ ἀπὸ δόξης οὐ
287 τῆς τοῦ νόμου ἀλλὰ τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος, εἰς δόξαν τὴν τῆς υἱοθεσίας· λουτροῦ
γὰρ τυχόντες εἰς υἱοθεσίαν ἐρχόμεθα. 2 Kor 4,1 Τὴν τῆς χάριτος λέγει, οὐ τὴν τοῦ
νόμου· διὰ γὰρ τὴν ὑπερβολὴν τῆς χάριτος τὰς θλίψεις πατοῦμεν. 2 Kor 4,2 Κρυπτά
ἐστι τῆς αἰσχύνης τὰ φαῦλα καὶ τὰ αἰσχρὰ ἅπερ οἱ πράττοντες κρύπτειν σπουδάζουσι
διὰ τὴν αἰσχύνην· οὐ γὰρ μετέχει παρρησίας τὰ φαῦλα, ἀλλ' ἐν σκότει διαλανθάνει. 2
Kor 4,3 Κἂν ᾖ κεκαλυμμένον τὸ εὐαγγέλιον, τοῖς ἀπίστοις κεκάλυπται, οὐχ ὡς ἐν τῷ
νόμῳ ἀπὸ παντὸς Ἰσραὴλ ἐκεκάλυπτο ἡ δόξα τοῦ προσώπου Μωϋσέως. 2 Kor 4,4
Ἐὰν μὲν ὁ θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου λέγηται συναπτομένης τῆς ἀναγνώσεως, καὶ τὸ
ἐτύφλωσεν ἀκολουθίαν ἔχει. ἐὰν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἐτύφλωσε, καθ' 288 ὑπερβατόν, ὡς τὸ
ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως, ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸ ἐγὼ
ἐσκλήρυνα τὴν καρδίαν Φαραώ, κατὰ τὸν ἀποδοθέντα λόγον. 287,ξολ2 Ὥσπερ δὲ
εἴρηται ἄρχων τοῦ αἰῶνος, οὐ φύσει ἄρχων ὤν, ἀλλ' ὅτι οἱ ἀπατηθέντες ἄρχοντα
ἑαυτῶν ἀνέδειξαν αὐτὸν ὑπακούοντες αὐτῷ, οὕτως καὶ ὁ 288,ξολ2 θεὸς τοῦ αἰῶνος
τούτου προσηγόρευται, οὐχ ὡς ἀληθῶς ὢν θεός, ἀλλ' ἀφ' ὧν τὰ ἔθνη λέγουσι καὶ
νομίζουσιν ὀνομαζόμενος θεός, ὡς καὶ τῶν γαστριμάργων θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καλεῖται. 2
Kor 4,5 Εἰ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκηρύξαμεν, φησίν, ἐνῆν ὑποπτεῦσαι ὅτι δολοῦμεν τὸν λόγον· εἰ
δὲ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καὶ τὴν ἐκείνου δόξαν, οὐδὲ εἷς δόλος ἐν τῷ κηρύγματι κατὰ τὸ
pass_a_gloss:
[Continues the 3:10 note: "nor would anyone say it has been glorified in this account] of the comparison toward what surpasses.
[Label 2 Cor 3:11.] He showed that the law must cease and be idle, and that the grace of the Spirit, brought in in its place, must remain.
[Label 2 Cor 3:12-14.] "Having therefore such a hope." The hope that is seen is not hope. And he made clear that grace remains, receiving its additions even after the resurrection. "Toward the sons of Israel not being able to gaze at the end of what was being done away": for as it was not possible to attend to the glory [a gap in the Greek], so they were not able to attend to the end of the law either, that is, that the law will cease. Straightway he says: "until today they have a veil." The end of the law, when the veil is taken away and they behold the glory of the Spirit, is that it is done away in Christ, that is, through faith in him. [Page number 286 dropped.]
[Second catena form, marked 285 col. 2 and 286 col. 2. It opens with a repeat: what hope? that the grace of the Spirit is not done away as the law is, but remains even after the resurrection. New material:] We, on account of the blessed hope of the grace of the Spirit remaining, teach with boldness, and we do not imitate the injunctions of Moses, who through the veil on his face signified that the Jews are not able to gaze and perceive that the law will take an end and be idle. The veil remains, not even showing a glimpse that, Christ having come, the law is done away.
[Label 2 Cor 3:15-16.] Just as Moses, speaking to the Jews, had the veil, but turning back to the Lord takes it off, so now too the Jews, after reading the law and giving back the book, carry away the veil, as though Moses had turned back to the Lord. So if, having withdrawn, you come to the Spirit, your veil is taken off, just as Moses' also was when he turned back to the Lord.
[Label 2 Cor 3:17.] The one deemed worthy of the Spirit of the Lord, this one has been freed from the condemnation of the law; for through the Spirit the gifts are worked. And the gift is toward the worthy.
[Label 2 Cor 3:18.] We, he says, the apostles, are seen by people with unveiled face; and saying "we all" he shows the benefaction of the Spirit to be common. And the glory of Moses was unapproachable for the Israelites, but for us the glory of God is easy to approach; for having fixed ourselves firmly in faith and having cleansed ourselves, we behold as in a mirror the glory of God, that is, we both see and take an impression, as in a mirror, in our souls of the image of the glory of the Spirit. From legal knowledge we are transformed into spiritual grace. Or it is to be understood thus: from the glory of the Spirit worked in us we come, plainly, into glory of adoption. [Column mark 287 col. 2 inside the sentence, dropped.] And "just as" shows "inasmuch as from the Lord the Spirit." And it must be observed that he called the Holy Spirit Lord, not the Son of God. And just as one person sees that mirror, and another receives the image of the one seeing, so also in the case of the Spirit; for those beholding as in a mirror the glory of Christ, themselves carrying away some likeness from the glory into glory, that is, draw to themselves and receive glory of the spiritual image.
[A second form, marked 286.30, repeats: we are transformed from legal knowledge into spiritual grace, and from glory into the glory of adoption. New material:] from glory not that of the law but that of the Spirit; for having obtained the washing we come into adoption. [Page number 287 dropped.]
[Label 2 Cor 4:1.] He means the one of grace, not the one of the law; for on account of the excess of grace we trample on the afflictions.
[Label 2 Cor 4:2.] Hidden things of shame are the base and shameful things, which those doing them are eager to hide on account of the shame; for base things do not partake of openness, but escape notice in darkness.
[Label 2 Cor 4:3.] Even if the gospel is veiled, it is veiled to the unbelieving, not as in the law the glory of the face of Moses had been veiled from all Israel.
[Label 2 Cor 4:4.] If "the god of this age" is said with the reading joined, the "blinded" also has sequence. But if "God blinded," by transposition [page number 288 dropped], like "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes for not seeing," and "I hardened the heart of Pharaoh," according to the account given. [Second-column note, marked 287 col. 2 and 288 col. 2, a different note on the same verse:] And just as he is called ruler of the age, not being ruler by nature, but because those deceived showed him to be their ruler by obeying him, so also he has been addressed as god of this age, not as truly being God, but named god from the things the nations say and think, as the belly also is called god of the gluttons.
[Label 2 Cor 4:5.] If we preached ourselves, he says, it was possible to suspect that we falsify the word; but if Jesus Christ and his glory, not even one deceit is in the preaching, according to the ... [continues in the next section]
pass_b_english: … of the comparison with what surpasses it.
On 2 Corinthians 3:11: He showed that the law must cease and lie idle, while the grace of the Spirit, brought in to replace it, must remain.

On 2 Corinthians 3:12–14: “Since, then, we have such a hope.” Hope that is seen is not hope (Romans 8:24). He made clear that grace remains and receives its increase even after the resurrection. “So that the children of Israel could not gaze at the end of what was being done away”: just as it was not possible to look steadily at the glory […], so they could not look at the end of the law either, that is, at the fact that the law will cease. At once he says, “To this day they have a veil.” The end of the law, once the veil is lifted and they behold the glory of the Spirit, is this: it is done away in Christ, that is, through faith in him.

The second catena form adds: Because of the blessed hope that the grace of the Spirit stays with us, we teach boldly, and we do not copy Moses' measures. By the veil over his face he signified that the Jews could not gaze and perceive that the law would come to an end and lie idle. The veil remains and does not show even a glimpse that, now that Christ has come, the law is done away.

On 2 Corinthians 3:15–16: Moses wore the veil while he spoke to the Jews but took it off when he turned back to the Lord. In the same way the Jews now, after reading the law and handing back the book, carry the veil away, as if Moses had turned back to the Lord. So if you leave and come to the Spirit, your veil is taken off, just as Moses' was when he turned back to the Lord.

On 2 Corinthians 3:17: Whoever has been counted worthy of the Spirit of the Lord has been set free from the law's condemnation, for the gifts are worked through the Spirit. And the gift is for those who are worthy.

On 2 Corinthians 3:18: “We,” he says, meaning the apostles, are seen by people with unveiled face; but when he says “we all,” he shows that the Spirit's kindness is shared by all. The Israelites could not approach the glory of Moses, but for us the glory of God is easy to approach. Once we have set ourselves firmly in faith and cleansed ourselves, we behold the glory of God as in a mirror: we see it, and in our souls, as in a mirror, we take the imprint of the image of the Spirit's glory. From knowledge under the law we are transformed into spiritual grace. Or it may be understood this way: from the glory of the Spirit at work in us we come, plainly, into the glory of adoption. “Just as” here means “inasmuch as it comes from the Lord, the Spirit.” Notice that he called the Holy Spirit Lord, not the Son of God. One person looks into a mirror, and another takes on the image of the one looking; so it is with the Spirit. Those who behold the glory of Christ as in a mirror carry away from that glory some likeness into glory; that is, they draw to themselves the glory of the spiritual image and receive it.
The second catena form adds: The glory we come from is not the law's but the Spirit's; for once we have received the washing, we come into adoption.
On 2 Corinthians 4:1: He means the ministry of grace, not that of the law; for because grace so far exceeds them, we trample our afflictions underfoot.

On 2 Corinthians 4:2: “The hidden things of shame” are the base and shameful deeds that their doers work hard to hide because they are ashamed. Base deeds have no part in openness; they slip by unnoticed in the dark.
On 2 Corinthians 4:3: Even if the gospel is veiled, it is veiled to unbelievers. It is not as it was under the law, when the glory of Moses' face was veiled from all Israel.

On 2 Corinthians 4:4: If “the god of this age” is read as one phrase, “blinded” follows in its natural order. But if the reading is “God blinded,” with the words transposed, it is like “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that they should not see” (Romans 11:8) and “I hardened Pharaoh's heart,” in the sense already explained. Just as he is called “ruler of this age” not because he is a ruler by nature, but because those he deceived made him their ruler by obeying him, so he is also called “the god of this age.” He is not truly God; he is called god from what the nations say and believe, just as the belly is called the god of gluttons (Philippians 3:19).

notes: 2026-11-11 claude-sumfix-b3: retranslated from the locked Greek. The old English was a word-order gloss and printed second catena forms in full. Doublets collapsed: 3:12-14 (first form kept; the 285/286 col. 2 form's new sentences printed under 'The second catena form adds:'); 3:18 (first form kept; the 286.30 form's new clauses printed the same way). The 287/288 col. 2 note on 4:4 is a different note and is kept. The Greek gap after 'the glory' in 3:13 is kept as […]. Labels one per note (3:11 to 4:5); page and column marks dropped; section opens and ends mid-sentence with '…' (the 4:5 sentence resumes in u02-open).
